title: Transport Coherence and Information Gain in Heterogeneous Reverse Osmosis Membranes Under Pressure–Salinity Trajectories
content: Reverse-osmosis performance is summarized by water flux and salt rejection, yet the same water-flux/permeate-concentration pair can arise from different combinations of selective-path conductance, defect passage, concentration polarization and compaction. We develop a self-consistent baseline–extended–full model for heterogeneous RO membranes that couples water and salt transport, permeate concentration, osmotic back-pressure, concentration polarization, selective-path compaction and pore-size quadrature. At 27.6 bar and 2.92 g L⁻¹ NaCl, EM gives 17.01 LMH, 0.1607 g L⁻¹ permeate concentration and 94.5% rejection. At the reference state, the reduced steric closure makes selective salt permeance 5.75 times more sensitive to the effective selective radius than hydraulic permeance, reflecting the squared dependence on the pore-radius–exclusion-length margin. Within the reference diffusive salt-transport closure, compaction increases the relative contribution of defect-mediated salt passage, producing a non-monotonic total salt flux over 5–58 bar and raising the baseline–extended–full model coherence-span ratio from 13.96% to 27.68%. Both pressure-dependent trends persist under two alternative compaction laws, whereas suppressing compaction eliminates the salt-flux turnover and markedly weakens the coherence-span increase. The turnover nevertheless depends on the salt-transport closure and its parameterization. Local Fisher/SVD analysis yields effective ranks of 2 at one condition, 3 under salinity variation, 4 under pressure variation and 5 under combined pressure–salinity operation at a 1% relative singular-value threshold. The fifth direction remains weak, falls below the 2% threshold and does not establish full practical parameter identifiability.
